clue.text: Fish on wet ground to be thrown back, schmuck!

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another is written after it
thrown back tells us the word for wet ground is turned round and read from right to left

parts.note: mud is wet, soft ground
the bass is a sea or freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone yells an insult at an angler throwing a fish back onto the muddy bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be thrown back' reverses the wet ground; in an across entry 'on' means placed after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are American slang insults for a stupid, contemptible person, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Throw shoe and run off

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A horse throws a shoe and bolts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges the seven letters of SHOE and RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: To unseat a rider is to throw them from the horse, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Cups carrying a fish, shade of green, one for old cricketer

indicators.note: a container carrying something holds it inside, so the other pieces go within the first

parts.note: a bra is the garment made of cups
a sild is a young herring, sold canned
olive is a dull yellowish green
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A recipe-like list of oddments: cups holding a fish, a colour, and then an old cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: D'Oliveira was a South African-born England cricketer; dropping him from the 1968 tour of South Africa caused a political storm. 'carrying' puts the other four pieces inside the cups.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil D'Oliveira played Test cricket for England in the 1960s and 1970s, so he is an example of a former player.

clue.text: After conclusions from barristers, you use delay

indicators.note: after places the following piece behind the letters just taken
conclusions are the endings, so the final letter of each of the next two words is taken

parts.note: to spend something is to use it up

explanation.surface: Once the barristers have finished, a judge's use of an adjournment holds things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conclusions from' takes S and U; 'After' puts them before SPEND.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend proceedings is to put them off for a time, a synonym of delay as a verb.

clue.text: Zero food required, provided plugs hole

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O

indicators.note: something that plugs a gap sits inside it, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: rice is a staple food
provided means on condition that, as does if

explanation.surface: No food is needed, so long as something fills the gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plugs' puts the condition word inside the food; 'required' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is an opening in the body or a vessel, a formal synonym for a hole.

clue.text: Blade good, cutting rump up

indicators.note: a piece cutting another goes into its middle
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the rear is the hindquarters or rump
pi is short for pious, hence good

explanation.surface: A butcher's good knife slicing up a rump steak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns REAR into RAER, and 'cutting' places PI within it; PI for pious is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender thrusting sword, so it is a kind of blade.

clue.text: Working independently, suggests slippery poisson?

parts.note: a slippery creature has got free of the hook or net
poisson is French for fish; the lance or sand eel is a small slender fish

explanation.surface: A self-employed worker is likened to an eel-like fish that has slipped away.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word is a playful way of saying fish; the sand lance is a small eel-like fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance sells work to many clients rather than being employed by one, so works independently.

clue.text: See 25
Speed management system cut corners, given oil spillage

indicators.note: a spillage scatters its contents, so these letters are thrown about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver who cut corners ended up with oil spilled everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spillage' rearranges the thirteen letters of CUT, CORNERS and OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruise control is the car device that holds a chosen speed without the driver pressing the pedal.

clue.text: So tail of halibut meets tailless fish

indicators.note: meets places the second piece directly beside the first
the tail of a word is its final letter
tailless means the last letter of the fish is removed

parts.note: huss is a name for the dogfish sold in fish shops

explanation.surface: The end of one fish comes up against another fish missing its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail of' gives T; 'tailless' cuts HUSS to HUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs meaning in this way or therefore, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Hurry off to hide piano behind back — it's rubbish!

indicators.note: to hide something is to put it inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: scram means go away quickly
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: back says the word just before it is read in reverse

parts.note: behind, as in behind schedule, means late

explanation.surface: Someone rushes away to stash a piano at the back, but it is junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hide' puts P in SCRAM; 'back' turns LATE into ETAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap metal is discarded metal, waste or junk, though it is often recycled.

clue.text: Fish from Algiers decapitated, then cooked

indicators.note: cooked means altered or prepared, so the remaining letters are rearranged
decapitated removes the head, the first letter of the city's name

explanation.surface: A fish caught off Algiers is beheaded and cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitated' leaves LGIERS, which 'cooked' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A grilse is a young salmon returning to fresh water for the first time, so a specific fish.

clue.text: Fish register into only vacant school of thought

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish of the carp family

indicators.note: into places the record inside the emptied word
vacant means the middle is empty, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: a log is a register or record

explanation.surface: Fish are entered into a register at a school, oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacant' leaves O and Y of 'only', and 'into' puts LOG between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideology is a system of ideas held by a group, which is what a school of thought is.

clue.text: Is envious of request, that of a Dickensian?

parts.note: to beg is to request earnestly
Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel, and the possessive form belongs to him

explanation.surface: Someone resents a plea made in the manner of a Dickens character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that of' gives the possessive RUDGE'S, the apostrophe dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent someone their good fortune is to be envious of it, the verb being a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Lightweight in split, rejected

indicators.note: in places the small weight inside the word for split

parts.note: to rend is to tear or split
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A small weight dropped into a crack is cast aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the small weight inside the word for split; 'split' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To have given up or disowned something is to have rejected it, a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: An expression of joy, perhaps, which can be positive

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem, and Beethoven's setting of the Ode to Joy makes it an expression of joy

explanation.surface: An outburst of joy might be a sign of positivity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the ode as one example of a joyful expression.
explanation.definitionFit: An anode is the positive electrode in electrolysis, though negative in a discharging battery, hence 'can be'.

clue.text: Small fishes' home smelt

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small in clothing sizes
pet fish live in a tank

explanation.surface: A small fish tank gave off a bad smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smelt' looks like the fish, but it is the past tense of smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Stank and smelt are both past tenses of verbs meaning to give off an odour.

clue.text: Change of heart in opera, grasping at musical work

indicators.note: something grasping another holds it inside
the central letter of the opera's name is swapped for another

parts.note: Tosca is Puccini's opera

explanation.surface: A character in an opera has a change of heart while seizing a musical work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of heart in' swaps the opera's middle S for C, and 'grasping' takes AT inside what remains. Tosca is Puccini's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuoso keyboard piece, so a type of musical composition.

clue.text: See 3
Net said to be fishy, however

indicators.note: something fishy is suspicious or not right, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone claims a fishing net looks suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be fishy' rearranges NET and SAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Both can mean as an alternative or nevertheless, in sentences like 'he chose tea, however'.

clue.text: Paul Kruger's first to enter requirement for a garden pot

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so these letters go into the word for what gardens need

parts.note: gardens need rain to grow
Paul is the setter, so he refers to himself as me

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the name is taken

explanation.surface: The Boer leader Paul Kruger goes first into a requirement for garden pots.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul is this puzzle's setter, giving ME; with K from Kruger, MEK enters RAIN. 'pot' looks like a flowerpot, but a ramekin is a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramekin is a small ovenproof dish for baking individual portions, a kind of pot.

clue.text: About to go wrong, cleaner lifted iron

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cleaner goes round the other piece
in a down clue, lifted means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Cif is a brand of household cleaning cream
to err is to go wrong

explanation.surface: A cleaner about to make a mistake lifts something iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' reverses the cleaner and 'About' puts it round the error word. 'About to' looks like one phrase, but the words do separate jobs; Cif is a UK cleaning brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferric means of or containing iron, so it matches iron used as an adjective.

clue.text: Trout was his — insert fish?

parts.note: read 'insert' as IN SERT: a fish, the chub, goes inside the letters SERT

explanation.surface: A composer's famous Trout prompts the idea of slipping in a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trout is a quintet and song by the composer. The wordplay splits 'insert' into IN SERT, so CHUB goes inside SERT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trout Quintet and the song Die Forelle were composed by him, so the Trout was his work.

clue.text: Some borders having identical plant

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outside letters

parts.note: identical means the same

explanation.surface: Some flower borders contain the same plant throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' takes S and E from 'Some'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame is an annual plant grown for its oil-rich seeds, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Fish among gar used in a stew with powerful associations

indicators.note: among puts the fish inside the other letters
in a stew means in a muddle, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the perch is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A fish cooked among garfish in a stew, a charged combination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a stew' gives SUARGED, the anagram of the two fodder words, and 'among' places the fish inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emotionally supercharged is loaded with strong feelings, so it carries powerful associations.

clue.text: Cheese with parent's fish — sole

parts.note: ma is mother, a parent, and the possessive adds S
the carp is a freshwater fish
sole means single, only one

explanation.surface: A dish of cheese with Mum's fish and some sole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' wants to be the flatfish; it means one.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascarpone is a soft Italian cream cheese used in tiramisu, so it is a type of cheese.

clue.text: In syrup I keep fish

indicators.note: in says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A cook keeps a fish preserved in syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: The fish is found across the words 'syrup I keep'.
explanation.definitionFit: The pike is a large predatory freshwater fish.

clue.text: Fish ate weed

parts.note: to have had dinner is to have eaten it
dock is a broad-leaved weed

explanation.surface: A fish has eaten some weed.
explanation.walkthrough: HAD for 'ate', as in 'had lunch'.
explanation.definitionFit: The haddock is a North Atlantic food fish of the cod family.

clue.text: Devoted, presenting a complete token of love

parts.note: to do a task is to complete it
a ring is given as a token of love

explanation.surface: Someone devoted offers a full engagement ring.
explanation.walkthrough: DO as a verb for complete, as in 'do the job'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoring means loving deeply, synonymous with devoted as an adjective.
